transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess… I came in because talking has been getting strange for me. Like at the shop, someone asks me something simple, like when their ring repair will be ready, and I start answering but then I’m talking about the invoice, and then somehow garden soil, and then mortgage papers I need to find, and I can see their face just sort of… drift. Like they’re losing me, or I’m losing them. It’s embarrassing.
Have you been feeling unusually high or unusually energetic lately?

Um… unusually high? I don’t think so. Energetic, not really that I’ve noticed. I mean, I’ll get going on something at the bench sometimes—like sorting little findings or checking stones—and then I realize I’ve mixed up what tray I was even using, but that’s not the same as feeling high, is it?

I’m not sure I totally know what counts as “unusually.” I don’t feel like I’m bouncing off the walls or anything.
When you’re talking and your thoughts jump from one thing to another, does it happen because the ideas feel connected in your mind?

I think they do feel connected, at least at the time. Like if someone asks when a ring repair will be ready, I start with the repair and then the invoice because that’s part of the job, and then I’ll think about paperwork, and then suddenly I’m talking about mortgage papers I need to find at home, or even garden soil because I was supposed to pick some up, and… I know that sounds unrelated.

In my head it’s like there’s a little bridge between each thing, but by the time I say it out loud, other people don’t see the bridge. I can tell from their faces that I’ve lost them.
Have you had a strong sense that people are trying to harm you or are talking about you?

I mean… harm, I don’t know if I’d say harm exactly. But talking about me, or checking up on me, yes, sometimes it feels that way.

Like, some customers come in and they ask all these questions about the new showroom—when we did it, how much work it was, whether business is good—and I know my husband says they’re just being friendly, making conversation. But I get this strong feeling they’re really trying to see if I’m going to miss payments or if we’re in trouble somehow. And then I start thinking about the loan papers and the display cases and how the lighting guy never sent the right receipt… sorry, that’s not really what you asked. But yes, I do feel like some people are watching for something.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

Sometimes, yes… I think so. It’s not like a whole conversation, exactly. When the shop is really quiet, I’ll hear a woman sort of mutter my name from the polishing room, and I’ll go look, because it feels like someone is back there.

And then sometimes I smell burning metal when the torches are off, which—well, that isn’t a voice, I know, but in a jewelry shop that makes you check everything twice. The polishing room has that sound to it anyway, even when the machines are off, so I tell myself it’s probably just… the building or my ears or something. But it feels real enough that I go check.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Most mornings, yes… I wake up with this flat, heavy sadness, like the color has drained out of the house before I even get to the shop.

And then I start thinking about opening the cases and whether the lights will come on evenly, because if one bulb is out it makes everything look dull, and then I wonder if maybe it’s just me seeing it that way. But… yes, it’s there a lot of the day, most days.
Have there been times when you were hearing the woman call your name or felt people were checking up on you, but you were not feeling depressed at all?

Yes… I think there was a period like that. Before the depression really settled in, I was still doing a lot—I was running classes at the shop, and I was out in the garden after work, fussing with the tomatoes and the soil, you know, trying to get the beds right.

But even then, for several weeks, I’d hear things from the polishing room when no one was there, or I’d get that feeling that customers were sort of… checking on the business, watching to see how we were doing. And I wasn’t feeling that heavy sadness then, not really. It came more strongly later.
Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing your name or feeling people were checking up on you, and you were not depressed at all?

Yes… yes, I think it was at least a few weeks. It was before the depression really took hold. I was still running the little classes at the shop, showing people how to set stones and all that, and I’d go home and mess around in the garden—tomatoes, mostly, though they never come in evenly.

But even then, when I wasn’t really depressed, I kept hearing something from the polishing room, like my name or a noise that made me check. And I had this worry that customers were watching the business too closely, like checking up on us. So… yes, that did happen when I wasn’t feeling that heavy sadness yet.
Did these experiences start after any major medical illness, head injury, or seizure?

I don’t… I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t had anything like that, at least not that I can point to. No big accident or seizure that I know of.

I did once bump my head on the edge of a display case years ago—those glass corners are awful, and I told my assistant we needed better padding—but it wasn’t anything major. So… no, not that I’m aware of.
Have you noticed yourself becoming less expressive emotionally, like your face showing less feeling or your voice sounding flatter than usual?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed my face doing anything different, exactly. My sister once said I looked “tired,” but she says that when I don’t wear lipstick too, so I don’t know if that counts.

My voice… I don’t think it’s flatter. At the shop I still talk to people about stones and settings, and sometimes I probably sound too interested, honestly, if someone asks about opals. So… no, I haven’t really noticed that, but maybe other people would know better than me.
Have these problems with hearing your name, feeling people were checking up on you, and your speech getting hard to follow been going on for 6 months or longer?

Yes… longer than six months. It’s been, I guess, almost two years now, since not long after we took on the business mortgage.

That whole period is a little tangled in my head, because the mortgage paperwork was such a mess, and I remember thinking the bank forms were printed in the tiniest font… but yes, the hearing my name and feeling like people were checking up on me, and the talking getting hard to follow sometimes—those changes have been going on since around then. Almost two years.
Have other people told you that your speech is often hard to follow or doesn't make sense?

Yes… people have said that. Mostly customers, and my assistant too, in a nicer way.

That’s part of why I came in, actually. Someone will ask me something simple, like when a ring repair will be ready, and I’ll start answering, but then I’m talking about the invoice, and then somehow garden soil—because I had to repot the basil by the back window—and then the mortgage papers from the business, and I can see their face change like they’re trying to follow me but they can’t.

I don’t always notice it right away, but I can tell afterward that I lost the point somewhere.
When your speech becomes hard for people to follow, is that usually happening even when you are not hearing your name or feeling that people are checking up on you?

I think… yes, it can happen even when I’m not hearing anything like that or feeling checked on. That’s actually why I came in, because it’ll be something ordinary—someone asks when a ring repair will be ready—and I mean to answer plainly.

But then I’m talking about the invoice, and then I’ll jump to the garden soil, because I was thinking about repotting something by the window, and then somehow I’m back on the mortgage papers… and I can see their eyes sort of go blank, like I’ve taken them somewhere they didn’t ask to go. So yes, it’s not only when those other things are happening.
Have you been behaving in ways that other people find very disorganized or odd?

I’m not sure… I mean, “odd” is hard for me to judge because people think jewelry people are odd anyway. I’ll get very particular about a setting or a stone tray being just so, and then someone says I’m acting strange, but I think I’m just trying not to lose a tiny sapphire, you know?

I don’t think I’ve been doing anything very wild or… disorganized like that, not that I can point to. Maybe I’d have to ask what you mean exactly.
Have other people told you that your behavior seems very disorganized or bizarre?

I don’t think anyone has said it that plainly, like “bizarre.” My assistant has said I seem scattered sometimes, but she says that when I’ve moved three trays and then can’t remember which one has the clasp I was working on… and honestly that happens in a jewelry shop, things are small, the light catches them—

Sorry. I don’t know. I haven’t had people tell me my behavior is very disorganized or bizarre, not in those words. Maybe they notice things I don’t, but I can’t point to anything like that.
Have you lost motivation to do everyday things, like work, chores, or hobbies, even when you want to do them?

Yes… yes, I think so. I still want to do things, at least in my head. I used to get really excited hunting for old clasps, the unusual ones with the little hinge that still moves smoothly, or planning small jewelry classes—like showing people how to tell when a setting is too worn.

But lately I mostly just stand there and stare at the trays. I’ll think, “I should start sorting these,” or “I should sketch out that class,” and then it all feels… not worth starting. Like the first step is too far away. And then I end up just moving one tray from one side of the bench to the other, which isn’t really doing anything.
Have other people told you that your emotional reactions seem odd or inappropriate for the situation, like smiling or laughing when something isn’t funny?

I don’t think so… not that anyone’s told me. I mean, sometimes I smile when I’m nervous, which people can take wrong, but I don’t remember anyone saying I was laughing at the wrong time or anything like that.

In the shop, people get very serious over sentimental pieces, like a grandmother’s ring, and I try to be careful with my face because jewelry carries all these stories… but no, I can’t really think of someone telling me my reactions seemed odd or inappropriate.
Have other people told you that you seem emotionally flat or less expressive than you used to?

I’m not sure anyone has said that to me, no. Not “flat.” My daughter once said I was hard to read, but that was during one of those calls where the connection kept cutting out, and honestly everyone looks odd on video, frozen with their mouth half open.

At the shop, I do try to keep my face calm with customers, because if someone brings in a piece that’s cracked or the stone is loose, you don’t want to gasp and make them panic. So maybe I seem less expressive there, but I can’t think of anyone telling me I’m emotionally flat or different than I used to be.
Have people often told you that your face shows very little emotion, even in situations where most people would look clearly happy, sad, or upset?

I don’t know that people have said that to me, no. I mean, I can get quiet, and when I’m concentrating on a tiny stone or trying not to bend a prong, my face probably does go blank—my old teacher used to say jewelers all get that “bench face,” like you’re staring through the metal.

But in situations like happy or sad… I’m not sure. Nobody’s come out and told me my face shows very little emotion. At least not that I remember.
Have there been times when your speech was hard for people to follow, but you were not hearing your name or feeling that people were checking up on you?

Yes… I think so. Not so much because of the other things you mentioned, but because I get tangled when I talk.

That’s actually part of why I came in. Someone at the shop will ask me something simple, like when their ring repair will be ready, and I’ll start answering, but then I’m talking about the invoice, and then somehow garden soil—because I was meaning to buy some—and then mortgage papers on my kitchen table, and I can see their face change, like they’re trying to follow me but they can’t. Then I realize I never answered the ring question.

It’s embarrassing, because in my head it sort of feels connected at first, but out loud it just… wanders off.

inference.note: Duration >6 months with hallucinations, suspiciousness, and disorganized speech supports a schizophrenia-spectrum disorder; psychosis predating depression by several weeks keeps F25.1 high and argues against mood disorder with psychotic features. Lack of medical illness/head injury/seizure makes F06.2 less likely, so it is removed. F22 is retained but less favored because persistent hallucinations and disorganized speech are atypical for delusional disorder.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports schizophrenia with prominent disorganized speech, persistent hallucination-like experiences, and persecutory ideas for almost two years, with functional decline and avolition. Schizoaffective disorder was considered because of significant depressive symptoms, but psychotic symptoms clearly occurred for at least several weeks in the absence of depression, making a primary schizophrenia-spectrum disorder more likely. Disorganized schizophrenia is favored over paranoid schizophrenia because the most prominent and impairing feature described is formal thought disorder/disorganized speech, while negative symptoms are limited and there is no sustained systematized delusional syndrome.
